heroHeadline: Gang Forces Seize Nan Brooklyn, Chancerelles, Delmas 2 & 4 Over Two-Day Offensive; MSF Cité Soleil Hospital Day 18 Closure; GSF Full Operations Set for June 1
heroSubtitle: On May 26–27, 2026, gang forces launched a two-day offensive in central Port-au-Prince, attacking Nan Brooklyn on May 26 (4 killed, 20 injured, homes burned) and extending their advance on May 27 to consolidate new leadership across Chancerelles, Nan Tokyo, Nan Barozi, Delmas 2, and Delmas 4 — a direct encirclement of the narrow government-held corridor in Port-au-Prince's city center. Witnesses alleged that police armored vehicles were positioned at the scene and that gang leader Jimmy Chérizier ('Barbecue') was transported to the area in an HNP vehicle, allegations unanswered by authorities. The two-day offensive directly contradicts PM Fils-Aimé's May 1 claim that gang territory had receded from ~90% to ~75% under early GSF joint operations. On the same dates, MSF's hospital in Cité Soleil — the only emergency health facility for the commune's ~300,000 residents — entered Day 17 and then Day 18 of continuous closure with no announced reopening timeline; Haiti had also registered 1,398 confirmed diphtheria cases as a secondary public health crisis intensifies within the collapsed healthcare system. The Gang Suppression Force (GSF) announced full operations would begin June 1, 2026, but its ~800-person advance force (of a 5,500-person authorized ceiling) remains exclusively deployed in Port-au-Prince's city center — providing no coverage for the neighborhoods attacked on May 26–27, nor for Cité Soleil or the Artibonite. Approximately 1.5 million Haitians remain internally displaced, and the Supreme Court ruling in Noem v. Doe / Trump v. Miot — which threatens to end TPS status for ~350,000 Haitian nationals in the United States — is now expected within weeks.
